== Biography ==
Philip Glasgow was baptised on 3 June 1711 at Uphall, West Lothian, Scotland, a son of [[Glasgow-1242|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Duncan-16665|Jean Duncan]].<ref name="Baptism">FamilySearch, “Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” Philip Glasgow, baptised 3 June 1711 at Uphall, father Thomas Glasgow and mother Jean Duncan, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-S7Z record VQ48-S7Z]. This is a derivative index entry.</ref> His structured birth date and place are estimates based on that baptism.

No reviewed record proves that this Scottish child later became a Dublin watchmaker. The Dublin records below are retained as evidence for a possible later identity, not as established events in Philip's life.

=== Two Dublin watchmakers ===

Irish records distinguish '''two Dublin watchmakers named Philip Glasco'''. The elder was established in Christ Church Lane by 1750, when a newspaper reported that Philip Glasco senior had married the widow Mangan of County Kildare.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/dc1719_52.html ''Dublin Courant'' extraction, 8 May 1750].</ref> His wife died in 1760.<ref name="ProjectSource2">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/fdj1725_98.html ''Faulkner's Dublin Journal'' extraction, 2 February 1760].</ref>

Philip junior of Christchurch Yard married Teresa Plunkett in 1768.<ref name="ProjectSource3">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/pg1758_74.html ''Public Gazetteer'' extraction, 17 September 1768].</ref> He died in Christ Church Lane in 1770.<ref name="ProjectSource4">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/dm1723_73.html ''Dublin Mercury'' extraction, 22 December 1770].</ref> The designation “junior” strongly supports two generations but does not formally name the elder Philip as his father. [[Glasgow-3932|Philip junior]] is therefore retained as an uncertain child.

The Dublin Gazette reported the death of the eminent watchmaker Philip Glasco in October 1772, and the 1772 will index describes Phillip of Dublin as a watchmaker.<ref name="ProjectSource5">[https://virtualtreasury.ie/ ''Dublin Gazette'', 6–8 October 1772, reference DGZ 1772/2547].</ref><ref name="Will1772">Virtual Record Treasury of Ireland, [https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PROI-DKPRI-26-7 1772 will index], Phillip, Dublin, watchmaker.</ref> These records identify the elder Dublin man, but do not connect him to the Scottish baptism. A separate FamilySearch probate index entry for a Philip Glasco in Dublin in 1777 is likewise a same-name lead rather than proof for this profile.<ref name="Probate1777">FamilySearch, Dublin probate index entry for Philip Glasco, 1777, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WGC9-DT2M record WGC9-DT2M].</ref>

[[Glasco-146|Phillip Glasco]] remains a possible duplicate of the elder Dublin watchmaker, not a proved duplicate of this Scottish child. No merge is supported without a record connecting the Scottish family to Dublin.

=== Dublin Glasco namesakes ===
Dublin records include Mrs Glasco in 1760, Mary Glascow in a 1747 probate index and an unidentified Glasco in the Rebellion Papers series. They belong to the wider Dublin Glasco research cluster, but none states a relationship to Philip and none should be attached as his wife or child from surname and place alone.<ref>[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/fdj1725_98.html Underlying record source: mrs glasco].</ref><ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx Underlying record source: mary glascow].</ref><ref>[https://irishmanuscripts.ie/womenshistorysources/index.php?whp_field=collection_code&whp_function=2&whp_searchterm=8830 Underlying record source: unidentified glasco].</ref>
